---
title: Storage access audit log
description: What the app-side storage access audit records, how long it is kept, who can read it, and how to roll it out.
---

## Purpose

Signed storage URLs are bearer tokens, and Supabase logs do not identify the
app actor behind a service-role request. Without an app-side record, an exposure
review cannot answer who obtained which object, when, and through which route.
`private.storage_access_events` closes that gap for the `workspaces` bucket.

## What is recorded

Each row is one access decision:

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `occurred_at` | Server timestamp |
| `actor_id`, `actor_kind` | User id (`user`), API key id (`api_key`), or none (`anonymous`) |
| `ws_id` | Workspace of the object |
| `path_root` | Lower-cased first folder under the workspace (`chats`, `docs`, …), or `(root)` for a root-level file |
| `object_id` / `object_hash` | Storage object id when known, otherwise the SHA-256 of the full object name |
| `action` | `sign`, `list`, `download`, `upload`, `delete` or `share` |
| `route` | Route template, for example `/api/v1/workspaces/[wsId]/storage/share` |
| `outcome` | `allowed`, `denied`, `invalid` or `error` (from the decision or the final status) |
| `item_count` | Objects covered by a listing or batch (0–1,000) |

- File names, query strings, IP addresses, user agents, emails and signed URLs
  are **never** stored.
- Only the actor id is personal data.
- To check whether a known object was touched, hash its full name
  (`<wsId>/<path>`) and compare it with `object_hash`.

### Instrumented routes

| Route | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/ai/chat/signed-read-url` | `sign`, one row per object |
| `POST /api/ai/chat/file-urls` | `list`, then `sign` |
| `POST /api/v1/workspaces/[wsId]/storage/share` | `share` |
| `GET /api/v1/workspaces/[wsId]/storage/share` (sign-on-read redirect) | `sign` |
| `POST /api/v1/storage/share` and `share-batch` (SDK) | `share`, one row per object for batches |
| `GET /api/v1/storage/download/[...path]` (SDK) | `download` |
| `GET /api/v1/workspaces/[wsId]/storage/list` | `list` |
| `POST /api/v1/workspaces/[wsId]/storage/upload-url` | `upload` |
| `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/[wsId]/storage/object` | `delete` |

Other storage routes are not instrumented yet. API-key requests rejected by
`withApiAuth` before the handler runs are not recorded. Add a route with
`withStorageAccessAudit` or `auditStorageAccess` from
`apps/web/src/lib/storage/storage-access-audit.ts`.

## Write guarantees and limits

The writer is `@tuturuuu/storage-core/storage-access-audit`.

- **Best effort.** `record()` returns immediately and never throws. A failed
  insert is logged with `console.warn` and dropped. The user request never waits
  for or fails because of the audit.
- **Bounded per instance:**
  - at most 50 rows per call;
  - at most 32 concurrent writes (extra events are dropped and counted);
  - identical `allowed` events from one instance are de-duplicated for 60
    seconds, so repeated image loads do not flood the table. Denials and errors
    are always written.
- **Losable.** Vercel Node functions have no `waitUntil` binding here, so a
  write can be lost if an instance is frozen right after responding. Treat the
  log as strong evidence when present, not as proof of absence.

## Retention

- Rows older than 90 days are deleted by
  `private.prune_storage_access_events(p_limit)`, at most 1,000 rows per call.
- The default-off Cron Control job `database-storage-access-audit-retention`
  calls it on the ten-minute trigger.
- There is no pg_cron schedule or Next route; see
  [Cron Control](/build/devops/cloudflare-cron-control#storage-access-audit-retention).

## Who can read it

- RLS is enabled with no policies, so `anon` and `authenticated` can neither
  read nor write the table.
- `service_role` can insert and select, but not update or delete. Only the
  retention function deletes.
- There is no product UI or API. Operators with database access query it for
  incident review.

Example (run with an operator role):

```sql
select occurred_at, actor_kind, action, route, outcome, item_count
from private.storage_access_events
where ws_id = '<workspace uuid>'
  and object_hash = encode(sha256(convert_to('<wsId>/<path>', 'UTF8')), 'hex')
order by occurred_at desc;
```

## Rollout

1. Apply `20261026120000_storage_access_audit_events.sql`. It needs approval and
   ships in the next migration batch.
2. Set `STORAGE_ACCESS_AUDIT_ENABLED=true` for the Web deployment. Until then the
   writer is a no-op, so the code is safe to deploy before the migration.
3. Enable `database-storage-access-audit-retention` in
   `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS`.

To stop writes, unset the flag. Rows already written stay until retention
removes them.
